sentences: University student the prince is accused of stealing the athletic funds.
Friend and fellow student the companion recommends he seek the assistance of classmate the detective.
Meanwhile, while honing his observational skills out in the countryside, the detective falls and is knocked unconscious.
A young woman passerby, the young woman, comes to his aid, much to his delight.
The detective accepts the case, and soon has a suspect, the thief.
The thief eventually confesses he took the money to try to get away from the crime lord; the thief is actually the son of a crook being groomed by the criminal mastermind for some later scheme.
Fascinated, the detective meets the crime lord face to face, impudently asking to study him, but of course the crime lord refuses to cooperate.
The detective informs the companion he has found his mission in life: to stop the crime lord.
Meanwhile, the prince's uncle, the count, arrives with important news: both his brothers have been killed in a "motor accident".
He is now the Crown Prince, and as such, cannot marry the sweetheart, the young woman's sister.
Heartbroken, the sweetheart commits suicide.
The detective is praised in a newspaper for solving a mystery that baffled the police force.
His investigative skills have failed to locate the young woman, but their paths do cross again.
The crime lord is after the sweetheart's love letters from the Prince for blackmail.
He has had her destitute sister the young woman hired as a secretary by "the
employer", actually a henchman named the henchman.

When the Prince asks the detective to take the case, he initially refuses, as he holds the Prince responsible for the sweetheart's death, but changes his mind when he learns that the young woman is involved.
The detective has the thief infiltrate the henchman's household as the new butler.

Through trickery, the detective gets the young woman to reveal where she has hidden the letters, but oddly, once he has them in his hands, returns them to her, even though she intends to publish them to avenge her sister.
He informs the companion that the letters will be the bait to lure the crime lord out of his lair.
For his part, the crime lord has become frustrated at being driven further and further underground by the detective's relentless pursuit of him.
He has the young woman brought to a "gas chamber" (where he has disposed of others).
The detective walks knowingly into the trap, but manages to rescue the young woman anyway.
The crime lord then sets his entire vast organization in motion to try to kill his nemesis.
The detective is up to the challenge, however.
Most of the crime lord's henchmen are captured by the police, and when the crime lord comes in person (in disguise) to do the job, the detective nabs him too.
The detective then plans his honeymoon with the young woman.

In 1890 the city, private detective the detective and his partner the doctor prevent the ritualistic murder of a woman by the nobleman, a noble who has killed five women previously and claims to have supernatural powers.
The inspector and the police arrest the nobleman.
Two months later, the doctor, engaged to his fiancée, is moving out of their lodgings and ending his partnership with the detective, exhausted of his eccentricities.
The nobleman summons the detective before he is hanged and warns him that three more deaths will occur and that he cannot stop them.
The nobleman is subsequently hanged and pronounced dead by the doctor.
The detective is visited by former adversary the adventuress, who asks him to find a missing man named the scientist.
The detective follows her when she leaves and observes she is working for a man who the detective deduces is a professor, and that he intimidates the adventuress.
The nobleman's tomb is found broken into and the scientist's corpse is inside his coffin.
Following a series of clues from the body, the detective and the doctor find the scientist's lab and discover experiments attempting to merge science with magic.
Later, the detective is abducted and brought to the temple of the order, a secret magical fraternity.

The order head the judge introduces the detective to the ambassador and the minister, and they ask the detective to stop the nobleman, a former member of the society and the judge's secret illegitimate son.
That night, the judge drowns in his bath as the nobleman watches.
The minister calls a meeting of the order and nominates the nobleman to take command of it, and the nobleman reveals himself to them.

When he explains his plan to seize control of the empire and reconquer the ambassador's country, the ambassador attempts to shoot him but bursts into flames when he fires his gun, and flees out a window to his death.

The detective studies the rituals of the order and recognizes that the nobleman's murders have been in accordance with their beliefs, and his final act will be to murder the members of the legislature.

With the aid of the inspector, the detective surrenders and is taken to the minister, where he sees evidence on his clothes to deduce that the nobleman has conducted a ceremony in the sewers beneath the legislature building.

The detective escapes and enters the sewers with the doctor and the adventuress, who find the nobleman's men guarding a device developed by the scientist, designed to release cyanide gas into the legislature chambers and kill all but the nobleman's supporters, to whom he has secretly given an antidote.

The nobleman comes before the legislature and announces their impending deaths, then attempts to activate the cyanide device by remote control; the adventuress is able to deactivate it with a controlled explosion and takes the canisters of cyanide.
The minister and the nobleman's supporters are apprehended as the nobleman flees the legislature.
The detective chases the adventuress and she leads him to the top of the incomplete bridge, where the nobleman incapacitates the adventuress and then fights the detective.

The nobleman falls through the scaffolding and the detective reveals he has deduced that all of his supposed supernatural feats were achieved through science and theatrical trickery, aided by the scientist's experiments.
A crane collapses, causing the nobleman to be ensnared and hanged in chains off the bridge.
The detective revives the adventuress, who tells him that her employer is the professor, and he is not to be underestimated.
As the doctor moves out of their lodgings, a police constable reports to the detective that a dead officer was found near the nobleman's device.
The professor used the confrontations with the adventuress and the nobleman as a diversion while he took a key component, based on the infant science of radio, from the machine.
The detective considers the case reopened.
On December 29, 1940, during the bombing of the city, the elderly doctor tells his nurse the an unrecorded adventure he shared with his late friend the detective.
On May 19, 1882, a royal treasury ship is destroyed by a monstrous giant octopus on the coast of the port town.
The detective and the doctor investigate the shipwreck and interview the sole survivor of the attack.
The inspector states that he has recently had contact with the detective's estranged brother the inventor, a fellow inspector who was paralyzed during a bank robbery.
In the poor district, a young man is killed by a Megalosaurus.
The doctor is skeptical until he and the detective discover the creature on their morning constitutional.
Finding escape, several more clues lead the detective to deduce that the monsters are artificial, built by a criminal genius to acquire resources.
On the case, the dinosaur steals a water pump operating a fountain and rolls of copper wire.
The detective reasons that the sea monster destroyed the ship earlier to acquire taxes from the colonies and the dinosaur stole the equipment to produce a bigger monster.
On one of their leads, the inspector is abducted.
The detective's deduction leads himself and the doctor to a castle in the seaside town, where they come across a masked mechanical man: the mechanical man.
The mechanical man is revealed to be the inventor, who also assumed the identity of a patient of the doctor's.
The accomplice, a robot disguised as a young woman, assists him.
The inventor explains that he built a cybernetic suit to cure his paralysis, the result of a ricocheted bullet fired by the inspector.
He plans to destroy the city, assassinate the queen and frame the inspector.
The accomplice travels to the royal palace with a bomb while the inventor pilots his most complex invention yet; a fire-breathing dragon in which he pilots and holds the inspector hostage.
The doctor is sent to stop the accomplice from killing the Queen, while the detective pilots another one of the inventor's flying inventions in an attempt to stop his brother.
The dragon sets fire to the legislature building and the abbey.
The accomplice is deactivated by the doctor moments before exploding and the dragon is sent crashing in the garden outside the Palace.
The detective shoots the inventor dead and proves the inspector was not responsible for the inventor's injury.
The inspector takes credit for saving the Queen and the detective and the doctor vow never to speak of the events again.
In present time, the doctor expires peacefully and his nurse visits his grave.
Nearby, the accomplice is visiting the grave of the inventor.
In November 1903, young women are being killed in the city, each with a silk stocking stuffed down her throat.
The doctor seeks help from the retired and disenchanted detective, who determines that the victims are well-born ladies, not prostitutes.
Evidence found includes a thumbprint, a pair of ladies' dancing shoes, broken glass, a strong smell of chloroform and a silk stocking removed from a victim's gullet.
It seems that the killer has a foot fetish.

The detective questions a survivor – a young girl who was apparently set free by her captor because she has a club foot – and arranges for her to "accidentally" see the footman that he suspects is the killer, despite his ironclad alibis.
The girl identifies him as her kidnapper, but the thumbprint clears the suspect.
The detective then baits a trap for the killer: he uses the sister of a victim and has her perform in a classical tableau at an event attended by the King and Queen.
Her Grecian-Roman costume is revealing, and her sandals expose her feet.
After the performance, she walks away to be alone; the suspect drugs her and is quickly caught by the detective and placed in custody.
The sister returns home and is tucked into bed by her father.
However, the suspect's thumbprint doesn't match the evidence.
The detective suspects the killer has an identical twin, and that the real killer is still on the loose.
The detective telephones the father of the "bait" sister to warn him, but the real killer has kidnapped her from her bed just minutes earlier.
The viewer sees the killer carrying her over his shoulder as blood drips from her face, where he cut her with broken glass.
The police force the other twin to lead them to his brother, but he escapes the police.

The detective finds the killer and his victim just in time; the young woman has a silk stocking tied around her neck, and the doctor has to cut it and perform something that looks like CPR, which was known in similar form from the late-18th century but did not come into standardised common usage until the mid-20th century.
The detective gets the killer twin to confess that he wanted his victims' attention, because they looked at him while in captivity.
Both twins are then taken into custody.
At the end, the doctor marries his fiancée the bride, an American psychoanalyst who had aided in the investigation.
They leave on honeymoon, and the detective is left sitting alone at the table.
The great detective the detective and his trusted companion the doctor travel to the American city to investigate a recent threat made by the professor.

During their investigation, the detective and the doctor are reunited with their old acquaintance the singer, now a popular music-hall singer, who reveals that the professor has kidnapped her young son the boy.

The professor has also left a note for the detective informing him that he will be approached by the police soon for aid in a crime, and should he not refuse – the professor also informing him that he should provide no reason for his refusal – the boy will die.

The detective is subsequently contacted by the city police regarding the recent apparent theft of the international gold exchange at the American city bank, with the entire vault of gold bars having vanished seemingly overnight, the theft only secret until a planned transaction between one country and another country in three days' time.
To protect the child, the detective refuses the case, but a chance comment by the doctor inspires the detective to shift his attention to finding the boy to remove the blackmail card.

While the doctor departs with the singer disguised as the detective to draw away the agent the professor has assigned to watch him, the detective determines that the boy was tricked into cooperating with the kidnapping as an apparent joke, allowing him to find the kidnapper.

Investigating the vaults, and quickly ruling as impossible the actual removal of many tonnes of gold via a narrow tunnel in the time available, the detective swiftly determines what has taken place; based on the speed of the lift's descent, it should take them 45 seconds to reach the vaults, but they stopped after only 42 seconds.
From this, the detective deduces that the professor had an empty, duplicate vault built a few meters above the real one, subsequently planting iron bars to stop the lift reaching the real vault.
While everyone puzzled over how the bars of gold were stolen from the false vault, the professor would actually be stealing them from the real one below.
In a final confrontation in the American city's underground, the professor escapes.
The case is solved.
As the detective and the singer say their goodbyes, the singer comments that her son has a keen intellect and a certain knack for solving puzzles, implying that the detective may be his father.
The two nevertheless part ways with the singer giving the detective a picture of her son to keep.
The courier, a British secret agent carrying a vital secret document, is murdered on his way to deliver it in the overseas country. The British government turns to the detective for help.
He deduces that the courier converted the document to microfilm.
Avoiding an assassination attempt, he hurries to the capital city, with the doctor to retrieve it before it falls into the hands of an "international spy ring".
The detective is certain that the spies do not yet possess the document, as people who were in contact with the courier on his journey have been harassed.
The courier's body was then delivered to the detective by the spies as a means to throw the detective off the track.
Before his death, the agent managed to pass the microfilm, hidden inside a "V for Victory" matchbook, into the unwitting hands of capital city debutante and bride-to-be the socialite.

The matches get passed from hand to hand at a party, unknowingly, and end up in the inadvertent possession of the chief spy, the spymaster (known as the seemingly respectable gentleman in the capital city), when he has the socialite kidnapped.
The detective tracks down the ring to an antiques shop, where he confronts the spymaster.
During their cat-and-mouse conversation, he even tells the spy that "the man who has it doesn't know he has it", with the matchbook in plain sight.

The detective is taken prisoner, but just as he and the socialite are about to be murdered, the police, summoned by the doctor by prior arrangement with the detective, break in and, after a gunfight, rescue the pair.
The spymaster gets away, along with the matchbook, however.
The detective races to the office of the senator, having led the spymaster to believe the microfilm is under a stamp of a letter in the senator's possession.
The detective arrives first and, as the spymaster eavesdrops, reveals the importance of the letter.
The spymaster takes the letter at gunpoint, only to have the police capture him.
The detective then takes the matches and sets fire to the letter, before revealing that the microfilm was in the matchbook all along.
In 1891, a series of bombings blamed on political radicals bring one country and the neighbouring country to the brink of war.
The detective narrowly intercepts one bomb that was intended for expert surgeon the surgeon, with the detective's former lover the adventuress playing a role in placing the bomb.

The detective grabs a letter from the adventuress and explains to the surgeon that the true culprit behind the bombing attempt is the adventuress's employer, the professor, who soon has both the doctor and the adventuress assassinated.
The detective discloses to his friend, the companion, that he has connected seemingly unrelated murders, terrorist attacks, and business acquisitions to the professor.

After meeting with his brother the elder brother at the companion's bachelor party, the detective meets with Romani fortune-teller the fortune-teller, the intended recipient of the letter he took from the adventuress, sent by her brother the anarchist.
He defeats an assassin sent to kill her, but she flees.
After the wedding of the companion and the bride, the detective meets the professor for the first time.
The professor taunts him about murdering the adventuress and threatens to kill the companion and the bride due to the detective's interference, while the detective vows to defeat him.
Soon, the professor's men ambush the companion and the bride on a train to their honeymoon in the seaside town.
The detective throws the bride from the train into a river, where she is rescued by the elder brother.
After defeating the professor's men, the detective and the companion travel to the capital and locate the fortune-teller.
The detective and the companion tell her she has been targeted because the anarchist is working for the professor and may have told her his plans.
The fortune-teller takes the pair to the headquarters of an anarchist group to which she and the anarchist belonged, and which has been forced to plant bombs for the professor.
The trio follows the detective's deduction that the next bomb is in the capital's opera house.

It is actually in a nearby hotel, where it kills several businessmen – a cover-up for the assassination of gun manufacturer the industrialist by the marksman, an expert sharpshooter and the professor's henchman; the industrialist's death soon grants the professor ownership of the former's arms factory in the factory town.
The trio follows the professor to the neighbouring country.
At the factory, the professor captures, interrogates, and tortures the detective, injuring his shoulder, while the companion fights the marksman.
The detective spells out the professor's plot, revealing that the Professor acquired shares in multiple war profiteering companies and intends to instigate a world war to earn himself a fortune.
The companion uses a cannon to destroy the watchtower where the marksman is concealed.
The structure collapses into the warehouse where the professor is holding the detective captive.
Soon, the detective, the companion and the fortune-teller escape.
Once out of the factory, the detective deduces that the professor's final goal will be to create an international incident at a peace summit in the neutral country.
He also deduces that the anarchist will be the assassin, disguised as one of the attending ambassadors, having been given radical reconstructive surgery by the surgeon.
At the peace summit, the detective and the professor meet on a balcony to discuss their plans over a game of chess.
The companion and the fortune-teller stop the anarchist's assassination attempt, but the anarchist is killed by the marksman.
Despite his war being averted, the professor remains confident in his victory, predicting to the detective that the nations of the continent will inevitably go to war with one another.

The detective reveals that, while being tortured by the professor, he replaced the professor's notebook that contained his plans and financing with a duplicate, whilst the original was sent to the bride, who decrypted the code using a book on horticulture in the professor's office, before passing the information to the inspector, who seizes the professor's assets and donates his fortune to charities for war widows and orphans.
The detective and the professor anticipate a fight, and both realise that the professor will win due to the detective's injured shoulder.
With the professor vowing to kill the companion and the bride, the detective drags him over the balcony just as the companion arrives, and the two fall into the waterfall.

Following the detective's funeral, the companion and the bride prepare to have their belated honeymoon in the seaside town when the doctor receives a package containing the elder brother's breathing device, which the detective briefly used before the summit.

Realising that the detective may be alive, the companion leaves his office to ask the bride about the delivery man; while the detective, having concealed himself, reads the companion's memoirs on the typewriter and adds a question mark after the words "The End".
Aboard a private aircraft, the diplomat – a parody of a real statesman – is on a goodwill tour of Middle Eastern countries.
He misplaces his diary and is thrown into a panic as, without the diary, he no longer knows what country he is about to land in.
Stepping off the plane, he extends greetings in Hebrew to a congregation of Arabs and is shot dead.

Soon after, the American President (a caricature of a real president) receives a threatening letter claiming responsibility for the death, signed "the arch-criminal", who claims to have set in motion a plan that will allow him to rule the world.
The president dispatches a top agent to the city to work with the world's top law enforcement officials and find a strategy to combat the arch-criminal.

Headed by an incompetent Englishman, the committee settles on contacting the detective, an eccentric private detective with an affinity for certain addictive drugs (a nod to the literary detective's experience with cocaine).

The detective is entrusted by the Commissioner of Police to find the descendant of the arch-criminal before he gains control of the world, accompanied by the descendant of the doctor, who is both a medical doctor and utter fool.
The commissioner is murdered while trying to leave, his death mainly the result of the doctor's rampant stupidity.
The duo then proceed to police headquarters to discuss the situation with the committee.
Before any plans can be made, most of the committee members are murdered by a sniper.

Without their help, the detective concocts a plan to invite the world's great detectives to a party, with the hope of laying a trap for the arch-criminal, who will be unable to pass up a chance at attacking all of them at once.

Many fictional detectives attend, including a hard-boiled private eye, a rumpled police lieutenant, and a fastidious sleuth, all of whom are dispatched while the detective and the doctor do a crossword.

The murderer is revealed to be an exact doppelgänger of the doctor, leading to great confusion when the detective cannot determine who is the real doctor, particularly when the doctor himself is too stupid to know which is which.

After some clever deduction, the detective discovers who the real doctor is, and the doppelgänger is revealed to be the arch-criminal's grandchild, who is in fact the detective's landlady the housekeeper.
Holding the detective and the doctor at gunpoint, she tells them of her long-simmering plan to avenge her grandfather's death by destroying civilization.

She shoots the doctor and proceeds to riddle the detective with (an impossible number of) bullets, which he survives, revealing he suspected her all along and so asked the doctor to load her gun with blanks.
As the detective gloats, the doctor sheepishly tells him that he forgot to switch the bullets; the detective realizes he's been shot for real, and dies.
After the end credits run, a narrator teases the possibility of a second programme, asking if the detective and the doctor will die, and the arch-criminal will destroy the world.
A voice replies "yes," and the first narrator says "oh."
In the dark alleys of the city, the notorious serial killer is committing a series of gruesome murders.

The detective and the doctor, already intrigued by reports of the serial killer murders, become involved when they receive a parcel from the district containing a case of surgical instruments with the scalpel, possibly the murder weapon, missing.
By a family crest on the box, they come into contact with the duke who admits his elder son the firstborn dreamed of becoming a doctor.
His younger son, the nobleman, tells them the firstborn has disappeared.
The detective deduces the instruments were pawned to a broker, the pawnbroker, who tells them that he received them from the woman, who gave her address as a soup kitchen run by the physician.
The detective and the doctor meet the physician, also a police pathologist, after convincing the inspector to let them view the body of the most recent victim, the murdered woman.
The detective convinces the doctor to go to the soup kitchen and make a fuss of looking for the woman.
A disguised detective then follows the physician's niece the young woman when she goes to meet the nobleman.
They explain the nobleman was blackmailed by a man who threatened to tell his father that the firstborn, who was helping the physician at the soup kitchen, had married a prostitute.
The nobleman now works there himself, also providing funds, but the firstborn was gone before he and the young woman arrived.
The blackmailer, the publican, now runs a local public house.
The Prime Minister asks the detective's brother to persuade his brother to investigate the serial killer case, unaware that he is already involved.
The detective and the doctor nearly catch the serial killer when he kills another prostitute who invites him into her room.
The detective confronts the physician who explains that the firstborn had learned that the woman had assisted the publican with the blackmail.
She and the publican tried to force the firstborn to add pressure to his brother to get more money, but he refused and the publican brutally beat him.
During the altercation the woman was disfigured when acid she tried to throw at the firstborn was accidentally thrown in her face.

The physician also reveals his crippled and mentally disabled assistant is the firstborn, seriously injured as the result of the beating from the publican, and perhaps the knowledge of what his wife had done.

The detective and the doctor discover the woman in the upper room of the publican's inn (in reality her property) and she admits that she sent them the surgical instruments, having removed the scalpel herself, to get them involved.

The detective and the doctor return the firstborn to his family, and the nobleman asks his father to allow the firstborn to stay, but he refuses until the detective reveals his condition and how much he has suffered.
The Duke softens and tells the nobleman to take the firstborn to his old room and make him comfortable and he will come to see him in a few minutes.
He asks the detective how he found the firstborn, and he tells him that he received information from the physician and the woman who owns the local pub.
During the night, the detective discovers the nobleman attempting to kill the woman in her room; he is the serial killer.
The pub catches alight during a struggle; the nobleman, the publican and the woman are all killed in the blaze but the detective escapes.

He explains to the doctor that the nobleman had no way of identifying the woman, who had besmirched the family name, so he killed every prostitute that he came across in the insane hope that one of them would be her.
With all those involved dead, the detective elects to keep the truth from the police.
The widower is an eminent judge who retreats into fantasy after his wife's death, imagining himself to be the sleuth, the legendary fictional detective.

Complete with deerstalker hat, pipe and violin, he spends his days in a homemade criminal laboratory obsessing over plots hatched by his (the sleuth's) archenemy the criminal mastermind, and pursuing clues throughout the city.
The widower's brother the schemer tries to commit the widower to a mental institution run by his friend the asylum director so he can get power of attorney and control the widower's finances.
The criminal to whom the schemer owes money is more than willing to get it by killing the widower so the schemer can inherit.
Psychiatrist the woman doctor's signature is needed on the commitment papers.

She insists on doing a proper interview and is immediately fascinated by the widower, who demonstrates a knack for what the sleuth describes as "deduction" (technically better categorized as abductive reasoning) as well as for hand-to-hand combat.
He walks out of the institution during the ensuing confusion, and the woman doctor comes to his home to attempt treatment.
The widower is initially dismissive of the woman doctor's attempts to psychoanalyze him.
He knows of the widower, who tried to make the world the kind of place it might have been and went mad.
“I am not that man,” he declares, and tests his logic on her with a scathing analysis of her lonely life, down to the fact that her suit is 10 years old.
But when he hears her name, he enthusiastically incorporates her into his life as the fictional doctor, the sidekick to his sleuth.
The woman doctor accepts the role of “chronicler”.

They begin an enigmatic quest for the criminal mastermind, following all manner of bizarre and (to the woman doctor) unintelligible clues and encountering a rich tapestry of people in assorted urban situations.
Eventually he takes her to the old friend, who thinks the woman doctor is deluded until she identifies herself.
He has known the widower for more than 30 years.
She leaves the widower there.
The next morning, the old friend wakes the widower, who fell asleep reading about himself in a biographical directory.
He asks the old friend which is his life, since he has no memories.
The old friend wishes he were the storybook hero.
The woman doctor rushes in declaring that the schemer wants the widower's money.
They'll find the criminal mastermind first and then deal with his brother.
The widower is energized: "I'm very glad you're here.
I like you very much."
At an abandoned building, they find an older couple who retired from the world in 1939 to grow magnificent topiaries.
The crook and his henchman appear.
The sleuth and the woman doctor escape by different exits.
They are to meet as prearranged at the woman doctor's small apartment at 7 pm.
The sleuth arrives late, by the fire escape, bearing flowers.
The woman doctor is wearing a white organdy dress with short puff sleeves and a pink satin sash.
Her dinner preparations have been disastrous.
They have a drink and he talks about going out together after this is over.
They are dancing when a bullet smashes the window, grazing his forehead and knocking him to the floor.
Distraught, she calls him "my sleuth."
The two head to the midnight rendezvous with the criminal mastermind.
The old friend and the other fascinating people they met earlier join in a brisk parade past the city landmarks.
They stop by a kiosk covering a manhole.
He tells his friends that the planet is shining under the soot.
He takes the woman doctor's hand and they descend into a tunnel.
The others do not follow.
A giant supermarket is a dead end.
